cases.question: How many annual leave days do full-time SaiTech employees receive?
cases.expected_answer: Full-time employees receive 24 working days of paid annual leave per calendar year.
cases.answer: Full-time SaiTech employees receive 24 working days of paid annual leave per calendar year [Source 1]. This leave accrues at two days per completed month of service [Source 1]. The number of annual leave days for full-time employees is fixed at 24 working days, regardless of the time of year they join [Source 1]. Part-time employees, on the other hand, receive a prorated allowance [Source 1].

cases.question: How many remote work days are permitted per week?
cases.expected_answer: Employees may work remotely up to three days per week with manager approval.
cases.answer: Employees may work remotely up to three days per week with manager approval [Source 1].

cases.question: What is the monthly home internet reimbursement limit in the Expense Policy?
cases.expected_answer: Eligible remote employees may claim up to INR 1,500 per month for home internet.

This limit is also mentioned in the Remote-Work-Policy.md, where it states that employees may claim up to INR 1,500 per month for home internet with a valid bill under the Expense Policy [Source 3].

cases.question: What are our standard weekly working hours?
cases.expected_answer: The standard work week is Monday to Friday, 40 hours in total.
cases.answer: Our standard work week is Monday to Friday, 40 hours in total [Source 1].

cases.question: Which reviewer is required for changes to authentication code?
cases.expected_answer: Changes to authentication code require a Security reviewer.
cases.answer: For changes to authentication code, a Security reviewer is required [Source 1]. This is because changes to authentication, authorization, cryptography, or data deletion require a Security reviewer [Source 1]. The author of the code change must also describe the behavior change and relevant test evidence [Source 1]. Additionally, the company has a security policy that includes guidelines for account security, such as mandatory multi-factor authentication for company email and source control [Source 2]. However, the specific requirement for a Security reviewer for authentication code changes is stated in the engineering guidelines [Source 1].

cases.question: What is the SEV1 acknowledgement target?
cases.expected_answer: The on-call engineer acknowledges SEV1 incidents within 15 minutes.
cases.answer: The SEV1 acknowledgement target is within 15 minutes [Source 2]. This is the time frame within which the on-call engineer must acknowledge SEV1 incidents [Source 2]. SEV1 incidents are defined as company-wide outages, confirmed active data exposure, or loss of a critical production capability [Source 1]. The acknowledgement target is part of the incident response policy [Source 2].

cases.question: How long do Atlas data export download links remain valid?
cases.answer: Atlas data export download links expire after 24 hours [Source 1]. This means that users have a limited time to download their exported data, and after this period, the link will no longer be valid [Source 1]. The data export itself includes projects, tasks, and notes, but does not include sensitive information such as passwords or authentication tokens [Source 1]. The expiration time of the download link is a standard security measure to protect user data [Source 1].

cases.question: What is the minimum password length in the SaiTech security policy?
cases.expected_answer: Use a unique password of at least 14 characters.
cases.answer: The minimum password length in the SaiTech security policy is 14 characters [Source 1]. This policy applies to systems that require passwords [Source 1]. SaiTech has a security policy that outlines various requirements for account security, including password length [Source 1]. The company provides guidelines for password management, such as storing credentials in an approved password manager [Source 1].
